Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
537 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Heat Advisory in effect for our southern counties (including the
  City of Houston) this afternoon. 
 
- Frontal boundary may bring isolated to widely scattered showers/
  storms later today / this evening, though a morning shower is
  possible in our northern counties. 

- Forecast has trended hotter for Sunday and especially Monday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1220 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

As of 12AM CDT, there are few things that catch my eye as I write
this AFD. Water vapor imagery is currently telling a story of a 
flow pattern in flux. The ridge that has dominated Texas weather 
over the last weak is shifting west, with the center of its ridge 
axis firmly over W CONUS. Meanwhile, a deep low over the Midwest 
is diving east to southeast, while its trailing cold front extends
all the way down into SE Oklahoma and N Texas. The airmass behind
the front is also of interest, featuring decreasing dew points 
and cooler temperatures. Me thinks the falling dew points are in 
SE TX's future....the cooler temps not so much. 

The HRRR continues to insist on a band of showers that develops
over our northern counties early this morning. The showers push
southward, fizzling out before reaching the I-10 corridor. Some of
the other CAMs suggest the presence of an isolated shower or two.
There does appear to be plenty of dry air in the 900-700 MB zone.
But ML water vapor imagery suggests there is slightly less ML dry
air in our northern zones. So I kept some PoPs in the forecast
north of I-10 this morning to give the HRRR a little weight in the
forecast. We shall see... 

This aforementioned front should continue its southward push, 
reaching our neck of the woods by later today or tonight. There's 
still some question regarding the timing of the front. Will the 
front be able to interact with peak daytime heating? Latest 
guidance suggest it won't arrive in SE TX until the evening, when 
daytime heating is being lost. Therefore, the chance of seeing
showers/thunderstorms has decreased but has not been eliminated
for later today. A veering wind profile ahead of the front will 
support a modest WAA regime when the air is already quite hot. 
Forecast peak heat indices from the I-10 counties to the coast are
generally 107-110 degrees, warranting the issuance of a Heat 
Advisory from 1PM to 7PM CDT in our southern zones. There could be
a sweet spot that's just inland enough to limit Gulf influence 
but also just coastal enough to limit mixing that manages to reach
111-112F. 

Sunday may feature some showers and isolated storms near the coast
and offshore in the morning. Otherwise, much drier air 
infiltrates the area in the front's wake. Mid/upper heights will 
be at their lowest on Sunday, generally supporting a cooler 
temperature profile. But drier air and the August sun should boost
temperatures into the upper 90s to around 100 (low 90s coast). 
Inland dew points are expected to be well down into the 60s, which
should keep heat indices below advisory criteria. The dry air may
not make it to the coast. So if you're in a coastal county, you
may remain in the humid soup. But on Monday, the ridge builds 
back into the region, warming the temperatures profile. With a 
similar dry LL regime remaining in place, Monday's actual 
temperatures cold get quite hot. Right now, we have high 
temperatures ~100 degrees across most inland areas. But this is 
technically a little "cooler" than most of the guidance. If 
forecast temperatures trend another 2-3 degree higher, then we 
could be approaching Heat Advisory criteria for actual 
temperatures (103+). The high heat may linger into Tuesday before
temperatures attempt to modify down to normal by mid/late week. 

Self

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 537 AM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Cluster of showers is currently moving southward towards our
northern terminals ahead of an approaching frontal boundary. This
band of showers is expected to dissipate before it makes it to the
Houston metro terminals. Additionally, low-end MVFR ceilings are
ongoing across the northern terminals (CXO and northward) and will
likely persist through 15Z. Can't rule out brief MVFR ceilings at
IAH this morning. 

High resolution model guidance has trended drier for this
afternoon. However, given that showers are already developing up
north, have decided to keep the PROB30's for showers in the
afternoon for IAH and northward. Further south, confidence remains
too low to include any SH mentions. A stray thunderstorm cannot be
ruled out either for sites with the PROB30's. Winds will start out
southwesterly this morning around 8-12 kt with occasional gusts of
15-20 kt possible this afternoon. Winds will become light and 
northerly behind the front. 

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1136 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Southwest winds 10-15 knots should gradually increase to 15-20
knots later today into tonight. For Galveston Bay and our eastern
Gulf zones, winds may gust to around 25 knots at times. Small
vessels should exercise caution later today into tonight. A 
frontal boundary approaches the area this evening into tonight, 
possibly resulting in a few showers and thunderstorms tonight into
Sunday morning. Westerly winds are expected on Sunday, followed 
by continued light to moderate south to southwest winds through 
much of the upcoming week. Winds may become more south-southeast 
late in the week. Seas should primarily be 2-3 feet, but could 
build to 4 feet (locally 5ft) Saturday night in our eastern Gulf 
zones. 

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
College Station (CLL)	  97  75  99  73 /  30  10   0   0 
Houston (IAH)			  99  79 100  78 /  20  20   0   0 
Galveston (GLS)			  94  82  92  82 /  10  20  10   0 

&&

.HGX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

     for TXZ200-213-214-226-227-235>238-300-313-335>338-436>439.

     afternoon for GMZ335-355.

     Small Craft Advisory from 4 PM this afternoon to 7 AM CDT Sunday 
     for GMZ335-355.

     Small Craft Should Exercise Caution from 1 PM CDT this afternoon 
     through Sunday morning for GMZ375.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1232 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal heat continues today with afternoon highs in the
  mid to upper 90s and maximum heat indices of 105-109F. A Heat 
  Advisory remains in affect for Jefferson and Hardin counties in 
  Southeast Texas from 1 PM - 7 PM this afternoon.

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region tonight
  bringing a 20-60% chance of rain across south central 
  Louisiana.
 
- Some slightly drier air will work into the region Sunday with dewpoints
  falling into the mid to upper 60s, but both high and low 
  temperatures will remain largely unchanged. 

- A few, diurnally driven, afternoon thunderstorms are expected to
  develop each day next week with daily rain chances in the 20-30%
  range. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Friday)
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

At the surface, high pressure is in the Gulf while a cold front is 
draped across the Ark-La-Tex from an area of low pressure in 
Illinois. Aloft, upper ridging is over the Four Corners region while 
a trough of low pressure is over the Midwest. As this trough 
progresses south/southeastward today, it will begin to broaden out 
becoming the main feature across the E CONUS as we head towards the 
second half of the weekend. As it does so, it will give the 
aforementioned cold front a further push south towards the coast. As 
this boundary crosses the forecast area this evening/tonight, a 
few showers and/or thunderstorms are expected to develop 
along/ahead of it, particularly over south central LA as it draws
closer to the coast. While this frontal passage will mean very 
little for us temperature wise, with highs still reaching into the
mid-90s tomorrow, it will bring a nice shot of slightly drier air
with a brief north/northwest wind shift tonight through tomorrow.
Tonight, especially as we approach sunrise, dewpoints are 
forecasted to drop into the mid-60s across interior SE TX and 
CENLA. Post sunrise tomorrow, further dry air advection is 
anticipated, with dewpoints at most locations (except near the 
coast) likely not getting above 70 degrees tomorrow. While in the 
grand scheme of things this is not really all that dry, for this 
time of year it should help things to feel far less oppressive 
tomorrow even as highs reach into the 90s. 

Moving into the work week, slow moisture return begins on Monday as 
winds turn back to the W/SW, followed by a more substantial return 
of moisture Mon night into Tuesday as the lingering boundary starts 
to lift off to the north. At the same time, E CONUS upper level 
troughing will begin to weaken and retreat northward, losing its 
hold over the forecast area by late Monday. It may leave behind just 
a slightly weakness aloft over the northern Gulf Coast, between 
ridging that will be slowly building in from the west and east 
simultaneously. With this synoptic set up, a few isolated afternoon 
diurnally driven showers and storms will be possible each
afternoon Tues through late next week. In addition, afternoon 
highs will continue to warm into the mid to upper 90s each day 
with overnight lows in the mid to upper 70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

A weak frontal boundary will move through the region this
evening/tonight causing winds to become more northwest to north
later in the period. Until then, breezy SW/WSW winds with frequent
gusts can be expected. This boundary may bring some isolated
shower activity to the Acadiana terminals tonight, but the
remainder of the terminals are expected to remain dry. Otherwise,
VFR conditions prevail.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

A weak boundary will approach the coastal waters later today, tightening
the pressure gradient overhead. This has already begun to result
in strengthening southwesterly winds, which will continue into
tonight. Tonight into Sunday, westerly winds will increase a bit 
further with sustained 15-20 kts and gusts to 20-25 kts as the 
frontal boundary moves through the coastal waters. The boundary 
will also increase thunderstorm chances late tonight through 
Sunday. An exercise caution statement has been extended through 
Sunday morning and a Small Craft Advisory has also been issued
through late tonight into Sun morning. Light southerly flow 
becomes reestablished Monday through the rest of the week.


&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue today. Rain chances will 
increase tonight into Sunday as an upper level trough and weak 
frontal boundary approach the area. A brief period of 
northwesterly winds are expected tomorrow, bringing some slightly
drier air into the region. Minimum RH's Sunday and Monday 
afternoons are expected to be in the 35-50% range. Winds will turn
back out of the south Sunday night into Monday. A few 
thunderstorms will develop each afternoon next week. 

&&

     for GMZ450-452-455-475.

     Small Craft Advisory from 4 AM to 10 AM CDT Sunday for GMZ470-
     472.

&&
